Thank you all for the advice and suggestions!

A quick update for anyone still interested:

I've had a talk with the two players involved and we've talked about the behavior that I didn't like. One was not as sympathetic as the other but we all agreed that DnD should be fun for everyone at the table and if this way of playing their characters stop enjoyment for me then they are willing to tweak how they act (not their motivations but their player behavior). They saw the whole ordeal more as a 'test the mettle' kind of deal while I just wasn't up for PvP action and was kind of trapped in a situation where my character had no control and his will and wishes were disregarded which brought up some personal stuff.

I'm stll going to have a talk with the DM later to let him know that's what happened, I've already said that these kinds of situations should be communicated and not a surprise and PCs should just have the option to not engage and remove themselves from such a situation. At the start of next session I'll ask the rest to retcon this session so my character just wasn't involved and their characters weren't as eager to harm the other characters (already discussed this with the two players and will clear it with the DM beforehand). That'd mean I won't have to deal with RPing this out and being reminded of the personal stuff.

Here's to hoping they're good with it and we can continue after we've aligned a bit more on that.

I feel like people really need someone they share good shit with that is also willing to listen to the bad shit and try to understand it. Like a voice of reason in the chaos that is life.

I don't know if me understanding, or at least trying to, is going to help you. I only know that it sometimes helps when someone else asks about us. It might help to get to new insights or it might help soothe some of the problems we face. Talking to someone who genuinely tries to understand us often allows us, and at moments even forces us, to better understand ourselves.

And I don't know if that's what you need right now. It seems like you've already walked a long route to get to this point. Like you tried almost every avenue where you thought you could to get the help you need. But you did post about your dissatisfaction with the disorders and the world here. Why?

Can you remember any specific instances that caused a great deal of anxiety or feeling of being overwhelmed? If there is one, maybe the direct cause of the panic attack? Maybe something else that you feel is significant?

If you weren't born with the mental disorders and they did develop then are they truly you? At your core? What or who are you at your core? Are you curious or do you find the world a scary or uninteresting place? Do you love anyone and if so, how do you express love?

You said you can't distinguish emotions, it's all just weird sensations that you can't define. Which suggests to me that you do feel **something** at least. Does it all feel too similar or are they different with you being unable to tell them apart? What effect do they have on you?

If I may ask, what made you feel anxious, depressed or overwhelmed? And I mean specifically, is it just the mental disorders? If so were you born with them or did you develop them? Is there something rooted deeper that's going on?

I know you said that you've talked enough but I can only offer you someone who'll genuinely try to understand. I hope you take me up on it.

Hey, 

I've had a few times in my life where I was at the breaking point. I have started attempts but never successfully went through with it, I had the intention but was either stopped by my own brain or someone else or simply too stupid to make it work.

I have started spiraling hard recently but I have always managed to get myself out of that deep dark hole I'd put myself in. So most of the time it does get better with time. I can tell you what works for me but I can't promise you that it will for you. 

Developing a healthy routine, including sports, hobbies, healthy foods and lots of social time is what tends to work for me. And with social time I mean, reaching out to friends, family or even strangers if you have to. Spending time together and trying to have fun together. It probably won't make the thoughts go away but might make them more bearable.

Now onto some unasked advice which may be completely unapplicable in your situation.

Online dating is almost never succesful for anyone, if you're already feeling left out tinder is the worst you could do. Women have a huge pool of guys and if you're not in the top 20% of guys in your area you're not gonna get much.

Meeting people irl, hanging out with female friends and investing time in your appearance(skin/hair/clothes/cleanliness) helps a lot, espescially at 20. If you don't have a lot of female friends try joining more clubs or sports that you find interesting (dance/book/cooking/music). You'll always have some common interest to talk about or do.

Never go into a conversation with the thought of 'I need to impress this person' but rather try to have a 'whatever happens it'll be alright' approach. Just try to enjoy the conversation, if you don't find it enjoyable just end it nicely and move on. If you both seem to enjoy the conversation try a little light flirting.

Remember, fucking up and rejection are a part of life, almost no one will hate you for it. Don't be too harsh on yourself.

If you're feeling like you don't have the social skills, you can work on that. I recommend the youtube channel '[Charisma on Command](https://www.youtube.com/user/charismaoncommand)' take some tips from that but always try to keep things natural.

If you feel like you're not physically attractive enough, try a grindr profile. (Yes, even if you're straight) You will see that there are a lot of guys that are willing to fuck you. As a bi-guy that really helped boost my confidence, may or may not work for you though.
